transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, what brings me here is... my talking gets all mixed up. Like, I try to explain things to people, you know? I try to tell them about the keys. The keys for the building where I clean, because there's this one set that always sticks in the mop closet door. And if you don't jiggle it just right, you're stuck. Reminds me of when I was in jail, honestly. The doors there, they have that heavy sound, that *clank*. But then I try to tell them about the prayer rug, because the pattern on it is so intricate, like a maze. A maze like a chessboard, really. The knights, they move in an L-shape, jumping over things. But when I try to explain all this, about the keys and the jail and the rug and the chess pieces... people just look at me. They tell me they cannot follow what I am saying. They say I'm not making sense.
How long have you noticed your thoughts and speech getting mixed up like this?

Well, let me think... how long. It's been about two years and five months, I'd say. Yeah, it started right after that brief detention... just a big misunderstanding at the building, really. They didn't have to make a big deal out of it, but they did. But that building, you know, the floors in the main lobby are terrazzo. It's a beautiful stone if you buff it right, but management buys this cheap wax now. Smells like fake lemons and ammonia. I can't stand the smell of lemons anymore. It reminds me of this bag of lemons I bought at the corner store once, and when I cut them open, they were just completely dry inside. Just hollow white pith. Pith... like those helmets, you know? The ones the explorers wear in the old jungle movies. I saw a movie on Tuesday where this guy was running through the vines, swinging from trees, and his hat never fell off. Not even once. I don't know how they film that without the hat falling.
During these past couple of years, have you had times where you felt unusually energetic, wired, or full of energy for days on end?

Oh, energetic... yeah. Yeah, sometimes I get so wired. When that energy comes, I just cannot sit still at all. I'll be at work and I'll clean the exact same hallway over and over again. I start moving all the chairs around in the lobby, making lists of things, and I just keep walking and walking even when my feet hurt so bad. 

My feet ache a lot because of these boots I bought. I got them at this army surplus store off 4th street, and the guy who sold them to me, he had a glass eye. You could tell because it just stared straight ahead while his other eye looked down at the cash register. Cash registers used to be so heavy, you know? Made of solid metal with those big buttons you had to really push down on to make them ring. Now everything is just a flat screen. You just tap it. Tap, tap, tap. Like a woodpecker. We had a woodpecker outside my window last spring, just drilling into the old oak tree out back. Making holes everywhere. Just endless little holes in the wood...
Does your thinking and speech get mixed up even during times when you feel your energy is completely normal?

Well, normal energy... yeah, I guess so. There are weeks, you know, calmer weeks. Where I'm not buzzing out of my skin, and I'm not dragging on the floor either. Just... normal, I suppose. But even then, even when I feel fine for like, more than two weeks straight... I still hear him. The man in the vents. He just keeps talking. And I know the people in the building are still signaling each other about me. I can tell by how they look. 

Looking... you know, I used to look at the vents a lot when I was a kid. We lived in this apartment with these big metal grates, and they would rattle whenever the heat kicked on. It sounded like a train coming through the wall. I always loved trains. The way the wheels click-clack on the tracks, it's a rhythm. Like music. I bought a harmonica once, thought I could play the blues like they do on the trains, but I just couldn't get the breathing right. You have to breathe in and out so fast. Like a dog panting in the summer. Summer gets so hot here, the asphalt just melts right onto your shoes. Ruins the soles. I had to throw away a perfectly good pair of loafers because the tar just wouldn't come off...
Looking back over these past two and a half years, would you say these periods of very high or very low energy have taken up most of that time?

Yeah, most of the time... most of the time since all this started, I've been in those keyed-up stretches. It's like I can't stop talking, and I take on these impossible cleaning plans, like scrubbing all the baseboards in the whole building with a toothbrush, and I just feel driven, you know? Like I absolutely cannot slow down. 

Slowing down... that reminds me of this old car my uncle used to have. It was a Buick, one of those massive ones from the seventies, painted this awful split-pea green color. He called it the Green Monster. The brakes on that thing were completely shot, so slowing down was always an adventure. We'd be coming up to a stop sign, and he'd just start pumping the pedal and praying. He kept a St. Christopher medal on the dashboard for luck. St. Christopher, the patron saint of travelers. My grandmother had a whole collection of saint medals in this little wooden box. The box smelled like cedar and old perfume, that powdery kind that sticks in the back of your throat. I swallowed a bug once when I was riding my bike, just flew right into my mouth...
